ledger.x: 28 November 1561: the Treaty of Vilnius creates the Duchy of Livonia.
1561: Russia holds Dorpat and Fellin inside the new duchy.
1566: declared a duchy under a Treaty of Union between Livonian landowners and Lithuanian authorities; Jan Chodkiewicz becomes the first governor (1566-1578), seat Sigulda Castle.
1569: after the Union of Lublin the duchy becomes a joint domain of the Polish Crown and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania; 'it had been a Lithuanian province until then'.
1582: the Truce of Jam Zapolski gives Dorpat and Livonia to Poland-Lithuania.
1582: the contest with Russia over Dorpat and Fellin ends with the truce.
1611: a truce after the death of Charles IX ends the war; the infobox gives 'status quo ante bellum'.
August 1621: Gustavus Adolphus's Swedes invade Livonia; the siege of Riga begins on 29 August.
January 1622: Valmiera (Wolmar) and several smaller Livonian castles fall to the Swedes.
1625: Koknese falls to the Swedes after a sixteen-day siege (landing in June 1625).
27 August 1625: Dorpat (Tartu) falls to the Swedes.
25 September 1629: the Truce of Altmark recognises the Swedish gains.
25 September 1629: the Truce of Altmark ends the Swedish-Polish struggle for Livonia.
25 September 1629: the duchy ends; the Commonwealth keeps the south-east as the Inflanty Voivodeship.

wars.name: Livonian War
wars.outcome: Russia gave up Livonia and Dorpat to Poland-Lithuania in the Truce of Jam Zapolski (1582); Estonia went to Sweden (1561, Plussa 1583) and Ösel to Denmark; the Order dissolved in 1561.

wars.name: Polish-Swedish War (1600-1611)
wars.outcome: Status quo ante bellum: the Commonwealth recovered Dorpat (1603/1604), Wolmar, Fellin and Pernau (1609); a truce followed Charles IX's death in 1611.

wars.name: Polish-Swedish War (1621-1625)
wars.outcome: Sweden took Riga (25 September 1621), Valmiera (January 1622), Dorpat (27 August 1625) and Koknese (1625) and kept Riga and Livonia north of the Daugava; the Truce of Altmark of 25 September 1629 recognised the gains.
